text:
alice_customer: Hey, hitting a regression with JSON mode when using streaming. Our client receives a truncated JSON object mid-stream and the parser errors. Happens intermittently (maybe 1-2% of requests) but affects a critical path.

alice_customer: Repro steps: we call /v1/generate with "stream=true" and a schema. Using Go net/http client behind our API gateway. Sample curl from our infra:

  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"x-structured-1","stream":true,"mode":"json","prompt":"..."}' \n    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

alice_customer: Received stream output (abbreviated):

  data: {"id":"resp-123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"value\":\"a\"},{\"id\":2,\"value\":\"b\"}]}}"}}]
  data: {"id":"resp-123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"\n,\"meta\":{\"cursor\":\"abcd\"}"}}]
  # connection closed abruptly here - last line cuts off mid-object

alice_customer: Parser error: unexpected EOF while parsing object. This started after a deployment last week. No 5xx errors from API.

emma_support: Thanks for the details, sorry about the hit. Can you confirm: do you see any 401/403 or token refresh logs at the time? Also which gateway (AWS ALB / CloudFront / internal proxy) is in front?

alice_customer: No 401s. We see a spike in 499/EOF at the gateway around the same minute. Gateway is CloudFront -> internal nginx -> app.

ivan_sre: Tagging. Two quick hypotheses: (1) proxied connection idle/timeout cutting the socket during chunked SSE, (2) client-level token refresh or connection reuse bug closing stream mid-chunk.

ivan_sre: Can you attach tcpdump / proxy logs around the timestamp? If not, try reproducing with curl from outside your gateway (skip CloudFront/nginx) to see if problem follows the path.

alice_customer: I spun up a quick curl from a public VM pointing directly at the Redwood endpoint (bypassing CloudFront) — still saw one truncated stream in ~200 requests. So likely not CloudFront specific.

mike_engineer: Rapid note from runtime side: we rolled an internal change that touches keepalive handling in our HTTP frontliner last week (roll 2021.4.8). Could be related. We're checking connection termination conditions when client closes early and how we flush SSE chunks.

mike_engineer: Also, structured JSON mode uses chunk framing to emit partial object pieces (we stream string fragments). If a chunk is dropped or the connection is torn down without sending final event or terminating frame, client-side JSON parsers will fail. We need to see whether the server closed, the reverse proxy closed, or an intermediate network reset happened.

emma_support: To help triage, please try two quick repros and paste results: (A) curl -N directly to our public endpoint with --http1.1 and --no-buffer, (B) curl -N through your nginx with connection: keep-alive and keepalive_timeout set high. Capture raw bytes for a failing run.

alice_customer: Will do. Also here's a raw capture from our failing run (snipped):

  \u003c== chunk (180)
  data: {"id":"resp-123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":1,\"value\":\"a\"},{\"id\":2,\"value\":\"b\"}],\"meta\":{\"cursor\":\"abcd\"},\"status\":\"partial\"}"}}]
  \u003c== chunk (22)
  data: {"id":"resp-123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"\n}\n"}}]
  \u003c== FIN from client (RST?)

alice_customer: The last closing brace chunk sometimes doesn't arrive; sometimes it arrives but then connection resets immediately after, leaving parser confused.

ivan_sre: Important bit: your capture shows a FIN from client. That indicates something on the client side or gateway is closing the stream after receiving what it thinks is enough. Could be read timeout in the client code or our service sending a terminal empty event that your client treats as EOF.

mike_engineer: On our side, server logs for resp-123 show that the model output finished and we sent the final SSE event: "data: [DONE]" followed by socket close. No internal error. Timestamps: last chunk sent at 2021-09-15T12:03:12.345Z, close initiated 2021-09-15T12:03:12.360Z. Small gap but within expected.

mike_engineer: Could your client be buffering and then issuing a pipeline request that triggers connection reuse/close? Also which HTTP client library and version are you using? Go 1.18+ has some defaults around TCP keepalive and idle connection reuse.

alice_customer: We're on Go 1.19 with net/http default Transport. We do not reuse connections for long-lived streaming endpoints; we open one per request. No explicit token refresh mid-stream.

emma_support: Another possibility: if the customer sees a billing/auth event (e.g., token rotation in our infra or throttle) at the same moment, the SDK might be injecting a synthetic event. Do you see any server-side auth revocation or billing enforcement logs tied to that request id?

mike_engineer: Checked billing and auth: no quota cut events for that customer at the timestamp. We do see two other requests from same CID that returned 429s a second before — but not this stream. Not likely billing cut midstream.

alice_customer: Repro attempt A (direct): 1000 runs, 2 truncated streams. B (via nginx, keepalive=120): 1000 runs, 7 truncated streams. Attached small sample of raw chunk bytes for one truncated case.

ivan_sre: That amplification via nginx suggests intermediate proxies increase failure amplitude. Could be nginx sendfile or proxy_buffering config swallowing small final packets. Try setting proxy_buffering off and proxy_http_version 1.1 + proxy_set_header Connection ''.

alice_customer: Switched proxy_buffering off and tested 500 runs — 0 truncations so far. This looks promising as a mitigation.

mike_engineer: Great find. This points to proxy-level chunk coalescing/timeout behavior. We'll add guidance to docs about recommended proxy settings for SSE/structured streaming. We'll also audit internal frontliner changes to ensure we always send a final sentinel event and wait a tiny grace period before closing socket.

emma_support: Action items: (1) alice_customer — keep running larger runs for 24h and paste any failing raw captures; (2) mike_engineer/ivan_sre — create ENG ticket to track runtime change + doc update.

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: rolled back 2021.4.8 -> 2021.4.7 to test retention of keepalive behavior (deploy id: deploy-2021-4-9-rollback).

mike_engineer: Logged ENG-2981: "SSE: ensure final sentinel and grace flush before socket close; guidance for proxy_buffering/nginx". Will include unit test + integration.

alice_customer: Thanks — mitigation works for us. We'll keep monitoring and will reopen if we see more. Appreciate the quick triage. :raised_hands:

emma_support: Thanks all. Marking this thread for follow-up in 48h. :hourglass:
